overview: After 4.cxb5 a6 White plays 5.f3, preparing e4 and a big centre while avoiding the main lines with Nc3 and Nf3. Black usually replies 5...axb5 or 5...e6 and gets the usual Benko compensation: open a- and b-files, a long-diagonal bishop on g7 and pressure on the queenside. White holds the pawn, so the game is a long-term fight between material and activity.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with e4, Nc3 and Be3, keeping the extra pawn
Return the pawn at a good moment to neutralise Black's pressure

black_ideas.idea: Open the a- and b-files with ...axb5 and put rooks on them
Fianchetto the king's bishop and pressure the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Benko structure with Black open a- and b-files
White d5/e4 centre against Black's queenside play

character.notes: Black gives a pawn for long-term pressure and White takes space in the centre, so both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: White keeps the b-pawn and Black has no forced recovery, only lasting pressure.

soundness.notes: The Benko Gambit is considered sound at high level.

structure.notes: Asymmetric pawn structure with half-open a- and b-files for Black.

approach.notes: Strong players play the Benko regularly.

level.notes: Plans are hard to get right more than lines to remember.

character.reason: Black gives a pawn for lasting initiative while White builds a big centre.
